seoTitle: How to Find 52 Week High Stocks in TradingView
metaDescription: Learn how to use TradingView's Stock Screener to find stocks near their 52-week high, apply filters, and confirm breakouts with charts and indicators.
intro: Finding stocks that are pushing to new yearly highs is much faster with TradingView's built-in Screener than checking charts one by one. This guide covers using the Screener with the right filters to surface 52-week high stocks for intraday, swing, or long-term ideas.

steps.heading: Understand 52-week high stocks
steps.body: These are stocks currently trading at or near the highest price they've reached over the past year, often used as a sign of strength.

steps.heading: Open the Stock Screener
steps.body: Navigate to TradingView's Stock Screener tool to begin filtering stocks by criteria relevant to 52-week highs.

steps.heading: Apply filters for volume, price, and market cap
steps.body: Narrow the results by setting minimum volume, price range, and market cap filters so you focus on liquid, tradable stocks.

steps.heading: Confirm breakouts using charts and indicators
steps.body: Once you've shortlisted candidates from the Screener, open their charts to check volume and price action around the breakout level.

steps.heading: Apply the results to your trading style
steps.body: Use the filtered list differently depending on whether you're intraday trading, swing trading, or looking for longer-term investment ideas.

faq.question: Is the Stock Screener free on TradingView?
faq.answer: Yes, the basic Stock Screener with filtering is available on TradingView's free plan.

faq.question: How do I filter specifically for 52-week highs?
faq.answer: Use the Screener's price-related filters to set criteria that compare current price to the 52-week high field.

faq.question: Why do some 52-week high stocks reverse quickly?
faq.answer: A breakout without strong volume support can fail and reverse, which is why confirming with volume and broader chart context matters.

faq.question: Can I save my Screener filters for future use?
faq.answer: Yes, TradingView lets you save custom Screener filter sets so you can reuse the same 52-week high scan later.
